target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28 with AWS SDE intern, Capital One SWE intern, Amazon contract work, and research; strong brands, but dense, heavily bolded AWS-service-heavy bullets.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Results arrive at the end of 3-line sentences after tech chains; several bullets (Amazon #1, #3, IEX all) have no outcome at all.
score_rationale.quantification: 90% satisfaction and 93% meal satisfaction lack sample/baseline; 34% speedup unclear vs what; IEX project has zero results.
score_rationale.technical_depth: Real decisions exist (precomputed index, decision gates, LSM vs B+ tree) but buried under AWS service chains that read as name-dropping.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Most bullets are 3 lines; 4-6 bold terms per bullet; 'with X + Y + Z' chaining makes every bullet a re-read.
score_rationale.skim_test: Brands pop, but AWS intern has one vague line and headline wins are drowned out by bolded technology names.
score_rationale.credibility: Five concurrent roles (AWS Redmond intern while contract/research/startup 'Present'); 'Engineered', 'Overhauled', 'scaled' puffery; satisfaction metrics unscoped.
score_rationale.ats_parseability: Clean extraction and standard headings, but phone is placeholder (XXX) and date formats mix 'June 2026' vs 'Sep 2026'.
score_rationale.visual_layout: One page and aligned, but dense, small type, bold noise everywhere, cramped spacing before EXPERIENCE heading.
score_rationale.domain_fit: General SWE evidence is there; Certifications above Experience and the thin AWS entry waste prime real estate.
score_rationale.overall: Brands will get interviews; the dense, bolded, tech-chain writing and overlapping 'Present' roles invite skepticism from a careful HM.

must_fix: Replace the placeholder phone number (XXX) XXX-XXXX with a real number or remove it.
Clarify: overlapping timelines — AWS intern in Redmond (Sep–Dec 2026) while Amazon contract, UMIACS research, and TerpLabs all show 'Present'; end-date or mark part-time/paused roles.
Clarify: the IEX project dates (Jul–Aug 2026) overlap the full-time Capital One internship; consider labeling it personal/side project.
Cut most of the bolding — currently 4–6 bold terms per bullet; keep at most 1–2 anchors (ideally the metric).
Bring every bullet to ≤2 lines; nearly every bullet currently wraps to 3.
Clarify: what the 90% and 93% satisfaction figures measure (survey of how many users, on what scale).
AWS intern entry has a single vague, present-tense bullet; either flesh it out with what you can state or acknowledge it as in progress.

bullets.quote: Researching and implementing Java-based utilization optimizations for Amazon
bullets.issue: Vague and thin for the top brand; what resource utilization, what approach?
bullets.suggestion: Clarify the kind of utilization (e.g., which component) and the technique being implemented, using only facts you can share.

bullets.quote: Overhauled the legacy UI of a test data
bullets.issue: 3 lines, tech chain buries result; '90% satisfaction report' lacks scope.
bullets.suggestion: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow editor in React/Electron + TypeScript with React-Flow and Jest-tested state validation; 90% internal satisfaction vs. legacy tool.

bullets.quote: Engineered a lightweight tree-style workflow search index
bullets.issue: Good design decision, but no result; Redis + Node IPC tail is noise.
bullets.suggestion: Built a precomputed tree-style search index over a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Python/SQLAlchemy) to minimize DB queries under access constraints, with Redis caching for full workflow retrieval.

bullets.quote: Developed a Claude skill for workflow generation,
bullets.issue: Strong metric buried at end of 3 lines; lead with the decision and result.
bullets.suggestion: Cut workflow-generation time 65% (to <15s) by building a Claude skill with sub-skill decomposition and Python search/validation tools; located bottlenecks via CloudWatch/OpenSearch latency logs.

bullets.quote: Deployed an Amazon Leo space topic research
bullets.issue: Reads as deployment-tech list; what the utility does and who uses it is unclear.
bullets.suggestion: Shipped a space-topic research tool adopted into Amazon Leo's ecosystem; defined infra in AWS CDK (TypeScript) with Fargate + GitHub Actions so unfamiliar engineers could contribute.

bullets.quote: Achieved a 34% speedup on a pipeline routing
bullets.issue: Speedup baseline unclear (throughput? latency? vs prior design?); trailing API Gateway clause is filler.
bullets.suggestion: Sped up a 6,000+ document inference-routing pipeline 34% by moving processing to Kinesis streams feeding Lambda workers. (Clarify what was 34% faster and vs. what.)

bullets.quote: Integrated automated fine-tuning of an AWS Bedrock
bullets.issue: AWS service soup with no outcome; the decision-gate idea is the interesting part.
bullets.suggestion: Automated retraining of a Bedrock source-relevancy model via EventBridge triggers with decision gates to skip redundant runs; added X-Ray tracing and SNS failure alerts.

bullets.quote: Developing automated training for PhysTwin, a physics-based
bullets.issue: Task statement only; what did you build or automate?
bullets.suggestion: Clarify your concrete contribution to PhysTwin training automation; keep the ICLR-targeted PhD team context.

bullets.quote: Built a Python pipeline linking AnyGrasp multi-camera grasp
bullets.issue: Model name string is noise; 'develop changes faster' is vague.
bullets.suggestion: Built a Python pipeline feeding AnyGrasp multi-camera grasp candidates as Open3D overlay views into a Qwen3-VL model, letting researchers iterate on isolated scene components.

bullets.quote: Cut research-environment setup time 30% via UV
bullets.issue: Two unrelated ideas merged; psutil/Pytest tail dilutes the setup-time win.
bullets.suggestion: Cut research-environment setup time 30% with uv dependency pinning and Docker for reproducible setups; added psutil timing/memory monitoring and Pytest tests.

bullets.quote: Co-founded and scaled a 110+ member campus
bullets.issue: 'utilizing Jira/GitHub... agile' is filler; no HM cares about Jira.
bullets.suggestion: Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio that has shipped 5 live products; organize engineering teams with agile practices.

bullets.quote: Sustained 20,000+ site visits within the initial
bullets.issue: 'Sustained' implies scaling work not shown; traffic is a product outcome, not your engineering result.
bullets.suggestion: Built Tortuga, a UMD class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days; added Prisma SQL queries with Redis caching to cut database load and latency.

bullets.quote: Building a work-in-progress integration of a RAG meal
bullets.issue: Honest WIP framing is good; '93% satisfaction' needs sample size; 3 lines.
bullets.suggestion: Building (WIP) a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app: GPT-4o mini over ChromaDB + SentenceBERT recipe search; 93% satisfaction among internal testers.

bullets.quote: Implemented a C++-based order book simulation on
bullets.issue: 'contract-based plug-and-play design... enforced correctness' is abstract; what was enforced?
bullets.suggestion: Built a C++ order book simulator replaying historical IEX data, with a pluggable interface so storage/matching strategies could be swapped and checked for correctness.

bullets.quote: Wrote and evaluated paginated hash-based data storage for
bullets.issue: 'Evaluated' twice with no result; what did drift evaluation show?
bullets.suggestion: Clarify the outcome of the drift evaluation against IEX historical book data, if you have one; otherwise tighten to the design.

bullets.quote: Designed and assessed the performance of a time-based
bullets.issue: Great HM bait (LSM vs B+ tree, rdtscp, perf) but no finding stated.
bullets.suggestion: State which structure won and under what workload, using your measured results; that conclusion is the interview hook.

structure.change: Move the AWS certification below Experience or fold it into Technical Skills as one line.
structure.rationale: Certs are weak signal for SWE interns; it pushes your best content (AWS/Capital One) further down the page.

structure.change: End-date or label part-time the Amazon contract, UMIACS, and TerpLabs roles; consider labeling IEX as a personal project.
structure.rationale: Five overlapping 'Present' roles plus a full-time internship triggers immediate credibility questions.

structure.change: Limit bold to the metric or one key term per bullet.
structure.rationale: Bolding every technology makes nothing stand out; the eye lands on tool names instead of wins.

structure.change: Trim Technical Skills to tools evidenced on the page; drop 'LLM tooling (Claude, Cursor, Copilot)' and SQS/SNS under 'Security & Monitoring'.
structure.rationale: Mis-categorized and unbacked entries read as keyword padding to a careful reader.

top3: Rewrite every bullet to ≤2 lines in What → How → Result order, cutting trailing tech chains and reducing bold to 1–2 anchors per bullet.
Clarify: the overlapping 'Present' timelines (AWS Redmond intern vs. Amazon contract, UMIACS, TerpLabs, and the IEX project during Capital One) so the page survives HM scrutiny.

Give the outcome-less bullets (AWS intern, Amazon Leo deploy, Bedrock fine-tuning, PhysTwin, all IEX bullets) a concrete result or finding you can actually state, and scope the 90%/93% satisfaction metrics.
